title: Batch/cache auto-tuner: incident action plan, safe apply & rollback playbook
creator: Liam O'Connor
body:
Summary:

This ticket captures the post-incident analysis and the operational playbook for the batch/cache auto-tuner (the "auto-tuner") rollout that caused a transient cost spike and increased tail latency for a subset of hosted tenants on 2026-02-10. The goal is to codify concrete mitigations, add preflight checks, and provide step-by-step safe-apply and rollback procedures so future tuning runs cannot cause broad operational regressions.

Key outcomes in this document: root cause, immediate mitigations we applied, the proposed safe-apply checklist, automated circuit-breakers and guardrails, monitoring and alert thresholds, on-call runbook steps (apply/rollback), and a list of follow-up engineering tasks and owners.

Incident timeline (short):
- 2026-02-10 03:17 UTC: Scheduled auto-tuner rollout started (batch size and cache TTL changes applied to 12% of traffic across two regions).
- 2026-02-10 03:31 UTC: Observability alert: per-token cost increased by ~22% for canary population; P95 latency increased by 180ms.
- 2026-02-10 03:42 UTC: On-call engaged; traffic steering paused and canary group removed from auto-tuner.
- 2026-02-10 04:05 UTC: Hotfix deployed to revert auto-tuner changes for affected group; cost and latency returned to baseline by 04:23 UTC.

Root cause analysis (summary):
1) Over-aggressive batch-sizing rule: a new model-specific heuristic pushed batch targets 1.8x above historical medians for low-concurrency customers. This increased queuing on RPC frontends and caused higher P95 latency for some request shapes.
2) Cache TTL misalignment: the tuner increased prefix cache TTLs but incorrectly left stale-ttl markers on models with short-lived context, leading to ineffective cache hits and worse token utilization (higher compute per request).
3) Lack of rollout gating: our rollout pipeline allowed a single-stage canary with only resource-cost alerts enabled; it lacked concurrent latency and error-rate gates, and there was no automatic rollback threshold configured for cost regression.
4) Insufficient preflight simulation: the preflight harness used synthetic traces that did not represent the long-tail prompt shapes used by affected customers.

Immediate mitigations applied during the incident:
- Paused tuner jobs and disabled the new heuristics via feature flag (flag: optimize.auto_tuner.v2).
- Reverted batch-size and cache-ttl changes for the canary population.
- Manually increased frontend RPC concurrency limit for the affected shards to desaturate queues.
- Created short-term alert that triggers a rollback if cost per token + latency exceed thresholds for >5 minutes.

Proposed safe-apply playbook (high-level):
1) Preflight validation (local + staging):
   - Run end-to-end simulation with representative workloads (include long-tail prompt sets from recent production traces).
   - Confirm model-level cost delta <= configured threshold and P95 latency regression <= configured threshold in staging.
   - Smoke test KV cache hit ratios after TTL changes using synthetic prefix sequences.
2) Gradual canary plan:
   - Stage 0: dry-run only (no apply) for 6 hours, collect metrics.
   - Stage 1: 1% traffic for 10 minutes with automated metric comparison.
   - Stage 2: 5% traffic for 30 minutes.
   - Stage 3: 12% traffic for 60 minutes.
   - Stage 4+: increase in powers-of-two with stable metrics for 60–120 minutes per stage.
3) Automated gating: each stage must pass checks before progressing:
   - Cost per token delta (canary vs baseline) < 10%
   - P95 latency regression < 50ms
   - Error rate change < 0.1 percentage points
   - Cache hit ratio does not drop by more than 5 percentage points
   - No dependency (e.g., network) SLOs breached
4) Automatic rollback conditions (triggered by the controller):
   - Any gating metric fails for 3 consecutive measurement windows OR
   - Combined cost+latency regression persists > 5 minutes during a stage
   - Rollback procedure must be reversible within the controller within 2 minutes (initial goal).
5) Human-in-the-loop escalation: if rollback conditions are hit, the controller notifies on-call and pauses all further stages until a post-mortem is created and approved by the Optimize owners.

Safe apply and rollback commands (examples):
- Pause auto-tuner: rwinctl feature-flag set optimize.auto_tuner.v2=false --env=prod --region=all
- Roll forward/rollback changeset (controller): rwinctl tuner apply --changeset <id> --target canary --verify=false
- Emergency revert (fast path): rwinctl tuner revert --changeset <id> --scope=canary --force
- Observe metrics: rwinctl metric query --name "optimize.batch_cost" --window=5m --group-by=canary

Monitoring & alerts (new/updated):
- New composite alert: optimize.tuner.cost-latency-composite (triggers on combined z-score of cost and latency).
- Per-canary alerts: optimize.tuner.p95-regression > 50ms for 3 windows -> pause rollout.
- Cache degradation alert: optimize.tuner.cache-hit-drop > 5pp for 2 windows -> require human review.
- Dashboard: Canaries view with per-model delta charts for cost, P50, P90, P95, error rate, and cache hit ratio.

On-call runbook (apply path):
1) Verify metrics baseline and target changes in the canary dashboard.
2) Start Stage 1 with controller; monitor for 10 minutes.
3) If all gates pass, progress to the next stage.
4) If gate fails, trigger controller rollback and open an incident in Linear (tag: INCIDENT).

On-call runbook (rollback path):
1) Run: rwinctl tuner revert --changeset <id> --scope=canary --force and confirm controller reports reverted state.
2) Confirm client-facing metrics are trending back to baseline within 10 minutes.
3) If rollback does not restore baseline within 20 minutes, escalate to SRE lead and open a page.
4) Preserve logs, traces, and metrics snapshot for postmortem analysis.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket (must be met before merge):
- Preflight harness added to the Optimize CI that replays representative production prompt shapes (smoke and long-tail).
- Controller gating logic implemented and tested with synthetic canaries in staging.
- Automated rollback path validated end-to-end and verified to complete in <= 2 minutes in staging.
- Dashboards and composite alerts created and linked in the ticket.
- Playbook doc reviewed by SRE, Runtime, and Product and signed off.

Follow-up engineering tasks (owners listed):
- ENG-21348: Add long-tail prompt fixture set to optimize-test harness (owner: Priya Ramesh).
- ENG-21349: Implement controller gating thresholds and automated rollback (owner: Marco Alvarez).
- ENG-21350: Extend metric collection to include per-model cache-hit deltas (owner: Nora Patel).
- ENG-21351: Update release pipeline to require preflight gate success before auto-tuner job creation (owner: Samuel Green).

Notes on trade-offs and rationale: we prefer tighter canaries and slightly slower rollouts over short-term cost wins because the platform-level impact of a misapplied tuning change is broader than a single tenant cost delta. The playbook errs on explicit, measurable gates to reduce ambiguity during noisy production events.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Maya Chen: Initial draft of playbook posted. Need confirmation from SRE on the 2-minute rollback SLA and whether controller metrics expose z-score calculation.
2026-02-18 - Arjun Mehta (SRE): 2-minute target is achievable if controller uses the cached state; we'll add a 30s pacing window to avoid thrashing on small oscillations.
2026-02-25 - Product (Sasha Kim): Recommend adding a customer communication template for tenants if rollback occurs (we should proactively notify customers with >10% traffic impact).
2026-03-02 - Marco Alvarez: Implemented staging gating logic and validated synthetic canary runs; attaching logs in links. Requesting review for merge to main branch.
2026-03-08 - Nora Patel: Added per-model cache counters to the metric exporter. Observed that one model family had intentional short prefixes; added exception list to the preflight harness.
